subject: sig_sotos_true.csv
text: The analysis found a perfect match to the Sotos syndrome signature, with an AUC of 1.0 and a Z-score of 125.4. All 500 submitted probes overlapped with the Sotos syndrome signature, giving a Jaccard similarity of 0.07 and 100 % probe coverage. The result is limited to the study itself and does not imply transferability to other studies. The runner-up was Claes-Jensen syndrome with a Z-score of 31.4. No data were missing or refused.

subject: sig_random.csv
text: A total of five hundred samples were submitted and all were present on the 450K platform, with most also represented on the EPIC v1 and EPIC v2 platforms. None of the twelve cohorts met the required criteria, so no matching disorder was identified. The analysis therefore returned a “no match” verdict, and no best-of-set guess was made.

subject: sig_sotos_flipped.csv
text: The analysis found a perfect match to the Sotos syndrome signature, with an area-under-the-curve of 1.0 based on all 500 submitted probes. This match is limited to the original study and does not imply it will work in other cohorts, and every probe’s direction is opposite to what was expected. The signature is present on all 450K arrays and on most EPIC v1 and v2 arrays, and it shows 100 % positivity in the Sotos syndrome cohort but none in the other disorders tested. The runner-up similarity was to Claes-Jensen syndrome, but with a much lower score.

subject: sig_tiny.csv
text: The analysis identified a perfect match to Sotos syndrome, with an area-under-the-curve of 1.0 and a Z-score of 26.3. All twenty submitted probes overlapped the known Sotos syndrome signature, representing 100 % of the submitted probes, though this may be a re-derivation rather than a new signature. The result is limited to the study in which it was derived and does not imply broader applicability. No data were missing, and the signature performed strongly across the platforms tested. The next-closest match was Claes-Jensen syndrome with a Z-score of 10.9.

subject: sig_low_coverage.csv
text: The analysis was refused because none of the 500 submitted probes were found in any of the reference cohorts, so nothing could be scored. All 500 probes were missing, giving a 100 % missing rate. Only a tiny fraction of probes were present on the EPIC v1 platform (0.4 %) and none on the 450K platform. The refusal code given was “insufficient_probe_coverage”. No matches or scores were reported.

subject: Silver-Russell syndrome
text: The analysis found no evidence of a band at the typical case score for Silver-Russell syndrome. The study used within-series controls and passed the structural confounding gate, with the interpretation made between studies. Out of two leave-one-study-out tests, one was computed, showing a sensitivity of 5/18 and a specificity of 6/6. The signature was built from 64 probes using data from 63 cases and 16 training controls across two studies (GSE104451 and GSE55491), and the overall verdict was graded.

subject: Sotos syndrome
text: The analysis found a strong association with Sotos syndrome. The result is limited to the single study GSE74432 and should not be applied beyond that context. The study included 38 cases and 53 training controls, using a published list of 7,085 probes. The quality check failed, and the overall verdict is that the finding applies only within this study.

subject: Kabuki syndrome type 1
text: The analysis found no evidence of a typical case pattern for Kabuki syndrome type 1. The study used data from two sources, GSE116300 and GSE97362, with 37 cases and 20 training controls, and built a signature from 278 probes. The result is graded and the interpretation applies between studies, with the structural gate passing and the controls taken from within the series. No leave-one-study-out directions were computed.

subject: Down syndrome
text: The analysis was performed on a single study of Down syndrome and used 29 cases and an equal number of training controls. A signature based on 3,753 probes was successfully built from rederived, unpublished data. The result is considered moderate in typical cases, but the confounding gate failed. The interpretation is limited to within-study use only. No additional leave-one-subject-out directions were computed.

subject: Coffin-Siris syndrome
text: The analysis gave a moderate band-at-typical-case score for Coffin-Siris syndrome. The result is limited to the single study GSE116992 and should be interpreted only within that study. The signature was built from 8,053 probes using 21 cases and 27 training controls, and it was derived from a re-derived, not published, source. The confounding gate failed, and the interpretation scope is restricted to the study. No leave-one-subject-out directions were computed.

subject: Williams syndrome
text: The analysis was performed on a single study (GSE66552) that included 20 cases of Williams syndrome and 15 training controls from within the same series. A gene-expression signature was built using 9,537 probes, derived anew rather than from a published source. The overall result was judged to be of moderate strength, but the confounding gate failed, limiting the interpretation to within-study only. This assessment is considered a single-study verdict.

subject: CHARGE syndrome
text: The analysis supports a link to CHARGE syndrome, but the confounding gate failed. The result is limited to the single study GSE97362 and should be interpreted only within that study. The signature was built from 907 probes using data from 19 cases and 29 training controls, all drawn from within the same series. This finding is not intended for broader clinical use.

subject: Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome
text: The analysis provides supporting evidence for Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome, but the interpretation is limited to the study itself. The result was derived from two studies, GSE116992 and GSE125367, using a signature of 4,911 probes built from cross-series controls. Sixteen cases were examined, with 27 training controls, and the signature was successfully constructed. No leave-one-study-out directions were computed, and the overall verdict is graded.

subject: ICF syndrome
text: The analysis gave a moderate score for the typical case. The study used ten training controls from within the same series and examined fifteen cases, with a signature built from 7,740 probes that was rederived and not published. The result is limited to this single study (GSE95040) and is intended for use only within the study. The confounding gate failed, meaning the result cannot be applied beyond the study’s scope.

subject: 7q11.23 duplication syndrome
text: The analysis was performed on a moderate-scoring case of 7q11.23 duplication syndrome using data from a single study (GSE66552). The result is limited to the study itself and should not be applied beyond that context. The test used 10 cases and 15 control samples, with a signature built from 1,827 probes. The quality check failed, and no leave-one-sample-out directions were computed. This finding is confined to the study and not intended for broader interpretation.

subject: Weaver syndrome
text: The analysis looked at Weaver syndrome using data from study GSE74432, which included eight cases and fifty-three training controls. Only one study was examined and no signature was built from the data. The confounding gate was deemed not-testable, and the result was classified as “too-few-cases”. Consequently, the interpretation scope is unavailable.

subject: Claes-Jensen syndrome
text: The analysis looked at Claes-Jensen syndrome using data from study GSE108423, which included six cases and twelve training controls. The test was deemed not-testable, and the result was classified as “too-few-cases”. No signature was built and no additional directions were computed. The source of controls was within the same series.
